message.content:
Desserts don’t have a single “color”—they come in a rainbow of hues depending on what’s in them. Here are a few common examples:

| Dessert | Typical Color(s) | Why |
|---------|------------------|-----|
| **Chocolate cake** | Dark brown (sometimes with a glossy chocolate glaze) | Cocoa solids give the deep brown tone. |
| **Vanilla ice cream** | Creamy white | Milk and sugar create a pale, creamy base. |
| **Strawberry shortcake** | Pinkish‑red | Fresh strawberries and sometimes a pink glaze. |
| **Lemon meringue pie** | Yellow (lemon filling) with a fluffy white meringue topping | Lemon curd is bright yellow; meringue is whipped egg whites. |
| **Red velvet cake** | Deep red | Food coloring (often beet or red dye) gives the signature hue. |
| **Pavlova** | White | Egg whites whipped into a crisp shell. |
| **Tiramisu** | Light brown (coffee) with a dusting of cocoa powder | Espresso-soaked ladyfingers and cocoa dust. |

If you had a particular dessert in mind, let me know and I can give you a more precise description!
